title: Haiti vs. USMNT—Concacaf Nations League: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackNov 13, 2026The USMNT faces Haiti over two legs in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/Getty Images/Catherine Ivill/AMAA rather peculiar few days beckon for the U.S. men’s national team, with manager Mauricio Pochettino remaining in charge for its Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal tie against Haiti, despite officially being appointed Manchester United’s new manager on Friday.

The USMNT is playing the ‘away’ leg of the two-match series on Saturday, although this match will be held in Miami due to a worsening security crisis in Haiti. FIFA’s 84th-ranked nation hasn’t been able to play on home soil for years as a result.
While Pochettino’s imminent departure and questions over the USMNT’s future will dominate the discourse surrounding their upcoming fixtures, there is still business to attend to.

After a promising World Cup ended in debacle then disappointment, Pochettino helped usher in the next generation of American soccer stars during the extended September-October break. The USMNT won all four of its matches, including victories over neighbors Mexico and Canada, both without conceding a goal.

Haiti, meanwhile, competed at its first World Cup since 1974 this summer but were drawn into a tough Group C. Still, the Central American minnows offered a respectable account of themselves despite failing to notch a single point.

The Haitians were defeated 2–0 by Costa Rica last time out, but that followed three successive victories at the start of the Nations League that ensured its progression into the quarterfinals. The aggregate winner of this tie will advance to next year’s finals.

The USMNT won all four of its matches during the previous break. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesDespite the circumstances surrounding Pochettino, the USMNT is still a huge favorite for this two-legged affair. While Haiti showcased plenty of pluck and grit at this summer’s World Cup, defeat for the USMNT here would be one of its great modern embarrassments.

This is a soccer nation that’s starting to expect, and anything but silverware in this competition should be regarded as a failure. There was distinct development under Pochettino, and the Argentine will leave the USMNT in a far better state compared to when he took the job on—assuming there’s no major upset here.
The heavy-hitters—Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie—are back for the Stars and Stripes, complementing a crop of exciting young talent.

Haiti has not beaten the USMNT since 1973. / FotMobThe “hosts” are looking toward the future after the World Cup, with stalwarts Johny Placide and Ricardo Adé both retiring. Leading goalscorer Duckens Nazon has also missed the previous two breaks, and his future with the team is unclear.

There is an absence of talent, which is what you’d expect from the 84th-ranked side in the world, yet there are a couple of familiar names, particularly to Premier League audiences. One of those, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde, is missing due to injury, though.

Alexander Pierre has established himself as Placide’s successor between the posts, and Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor will be expected to lead Haiti’s attack. His thunderous strike against Morocco was one of the best goals of the 2026 World Cup.
Haiti predicted lineup vs. USMNT (4-2-3-1): Pierre; Arcus, Duverne, Delcroix, Expérience; Jacques, Sainté; Deedson, Picault, Providence; Isidor
The USMNT is expected to walk away with victory. / FotMobThere have been a couple of alterations to Pochettino’s initial roster, with Sergiño Dest the latest to withdraw due to an injury.
George Campbell and Gio Reyna have also pulled out, being replaced by Mark McKenzie and Jack McGlynn, respectively.

Pochettino has the likes of Pulisic, Balogun, McKennie, Tyler Adams, Chris Richards and Alex Freeman available, but the Argentine will surely be tempted to trust the USMNT’s starlets before departing for Manchester.

Teenage sensation Cavan Sullivan is among those pushing for a start, while Julian Hall was in fine form during the previous break. Hall has the task of displacing Balogun, who’s already being linked with a move to United after Pochettino’s appointment was confirmed.
USMNT predicted lineup vs. Haiti (4-2-3-1): Kochen; Freeman, Richards, Trusty, Robinson; Adams, McKennie; Sullivan, Tillman, Pulisic; Balogun.
